title: Dual Macrophage Programs in Pulmonary Fibrosis: Functional Attribution and Spatial Resolution of Iron-Handling/Efferocytosis FOLR2+ and Scar-Associated SPP1+ Axes
content: Background: A dual-axis organization of non-alveolar macrophages—scar-associated SPP1+ and tissue-resident-like FOLR2+ populations—was recently delineated in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), but their functions and niches remain unresolved. Methods: We integrated full-transcriptome re-clustering of the GSE135893 myeloid compartment, independent replication (GSE136831), and GeoMx spatial profiling of bronchiolitis obliterans and fibrosing ILD lesions (GSE316672, GSE255174). Results: Two IPF-emergent entities were confirmed and first systematically quantified: SPP1+/TREM2+ scar-associated macrophages (97% IPF-derived; 4.0% to 30.7% of macrophages) and the FOLR2+/CD163+/SLC40A1+ iron-handling population (95% IPF; 11.9% to 19.0%). Both axes replicated in the Adams cohort (donor-level p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ and 8.2 × 10⁻¹¹). Spatial profiling revealed a core-and-ring architecture in BO lesions (SPP1+/TREM2+ luminal core; MCL1-high scavenger ring). Monocyte flux correlated with fibroblast apoptotic priming (rho = +0.54; nominal p = 0.045). No canonical M1/M2a enrichment was detected; the FOLR2+ efferocytosis arm was MERTK/GAS6-dominant across cohorts. Conclusion: The fibrotic lung’s dual-axis macrophage architecture is functionally attributed and spatially resolved, with implications for combination targeting.
